findings.claim: html-css-js-final-mcq-25's stem conflicts with what the course teaches. The listed fetch sends a JSON.stringify body with no Content-Type header (line 200). The calling-your-spring-boot-api page's Activity 1 ('Predict a POST with no header') and quiz '::o1 string body type::' teach that such a POST goes as text/plain and Spring answers 415. Yet the stem says the response is 400. A learner who studied that page may stop on the mismatch, suspect a trick or spend time on the missing header, although the item's decision (the caller ignores save's result object) does not depend on it.
findings.recommendation: Add headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" } to the fetch call, or replace the options object with a comment such as '/* POST options */' so the listing shows nothing the course marks as a bug.

items.note: Resolved. html-css-js-final-mcq-01 (line 5) now steps over the extra pass of a 'for (let i = 0; i <= items.length; i++)' loop and reads the evidence, a TypeError on items[3], back to the loop bound. No debugging artifact.gift item, mastery item ('stepping and watching', 'stopping on the bad trail', 'reading the evidence') or page activity uses an off-by-one bound. I searched the learner pages and banks for '<= x.length', 'off-by-one' and 'length - 1' in learner text and found nothing. The idea that a missing index gives undefined and that reading .price on undefined throws is taught (arrays quiz '::o1 missing property::', the DOM page null-error activity). The 'Step over skips the line' distractor (line 10) echoes the mastery check's 'step over skips the line', but it is a minor echo, not the keyed decision.

Resolved. html-css-js-final-mcq-12 (line 94) is a new applied diagnosis: a Secure cookie on a plain-HTTP staging site, so later requests arrive without a session. The topic quiz '::o2 secure::' and the cookies page ('Secure keeps a cookie off plain HTTP') teach the attribute in the abstract. No practice item gives this symptom, and the HttpOnly, SameSite and localStorage distractors are each a real misconception with their own feedback. The key is no longer the longest option.

Still open. html-css-js-final-mcq-02 (line 14) keys 'An h3 with the same class' for a subheading under the h2 'Recipe'. That is the html-and-css mastery item 'semantic-html-page-structure o2 the next level down' (cards inside an h2 section use h3). Its distractors follow the mastery item's: 'h6, because the smallest heading level matches the small text' (line 17) is the mastery check's 'h4, to make the cards visibly smaller ... size is styled with CSS', and 'An h2, because every heading inside a section starts again at level 2' (line 18) is its 'h2, so the cards match the section headings ... need the next level down, not a sibling level'. 'Keep the class so the look is unchanged' is the semantic quiz '::o3 keep the layout::'. The only new element is that a styled p is not a heading (line 15), and the level decision the key turns on can be recalled from the mastery check. Key a semantic decision that no semantic quiz, mastery, page or Course Review item resolves. Heading level under an h2, number-as-size, class-keeps-look, aside for a side box and nav for a link block are all taken.

Resolved. html-css-js-final-mcq-19 (line 148) ports Java int division (7 / 2) and uses the result as a loop bound. The page teaches 'There is no int, long or double' and one Number type, but no activity, quiz or mastery item uses division or a fractional loop bound; I searched for '7 / 2' and 'integer division' and found nothing. Each distractor is a real Java-habit error (truncation, rounding up, or ignoring that 4 <= 3.5 is false).

Still open for item 30. html-css-js-final-mcq-25 (line 199) is resolved. It is a new caller-ignores-the-result bug that builds on the http-errors page's 'Return a small result object, so the caller decides what to show'. Items 25 and 30 no longer share a keyed decision. html-css-js-final-mcq-30 (line 245) still re-asks practised decisions. 'Show detail, not title "Bad Request"' is Course Review browser-client Activity 3 option D ('title only names the kind of problem, so the person sees "Bad Request" ... detail explains this occurrence') and the http-errors quiz '::o2 detail member::'. 'Insert with textContent even from your own API' is the fetching-data quiz '::o3 safe render::'. Its distractor 'Join titles into an HTML string for innerHTML, since it is your own API' is the misconception item 30's line 247 repeats ('innerHTML because it comes from our own API'). The instance distractor (line 249) is that quiz's 'closer to instance' option. The key can be picked by recalling those three items. Item 30 is now also one of the easiest items, yet it closes the test. Replace it with a handling-http-errors decision none of the five page activities, the quiz, the mastery item 'two broken mornings' or Course Review A3 resolves, at band 2 or 3.

Resolved. In html-css-js-final-mcq-03 (line 21), every distractor now depends on the gap or on fr. 'repeat(4, 225px)' (line 22) overflows only because of the three 16px gaps (948px). 'repeat(auto-fill, 225px)' (line 23) fits only three columns once the gaps are counted. '4fr' (line 25) is a single track. No option can be rejected without gap or fr reasoning, and auto-fill is taught (grid quiz '::o1 minmax and auto-fill::').

Resolved. html-css-js-final-mcq-06 (line 44) is new: a const object passed to a function that pushes and then reassigns its parameter. All three distractors are real misconceptions: the reassignment reaching the caller (0), reassigning the const (TypeError), and const forbidding mutation. The parameter-rebinding rule is not stated on a page, but it matches Java's pass-a-reference-by-value, which the audience already knows, so it is not an untaught prerequisite. It differs from the let-const page's Activity 1 and quiz '::o2 const object::', which have no function boundary.
